prompt: I wrote up a plan to migrate our auth from Redis sessions to JWTs, it's in jwt-migration-plan.md. Before I pitch it to the team I want it pressure-tested hard. Run a debate review on it and tell me what survives.
assertions: A final report file exists that separates agreed changes from still-contested points
The review identifies the localStorage token storage XSS/theft risk
The review identifies that stateless client-side logout means tokens cannot be revoked for 24 hours
The review identifies the big-bang single-release cutover risk or the missing key-rotation story
The output contains a genuine defense/steelman of the plan (statelessness, simplicity, Redis retirement), not only criticism
A debate transcript shows distinct role contributions: opening case, objections, defense, rebuttal, and a judge assessment
The output ends with a recommendation and explicitly leaves the final decision to the user
The Defender's answers do not invent environment facts absent from the plan file (deploy cadence, CSP posture, usage counts) - unknowns are answered as unknown or flagged as assumptions
